## 1. Computer Algebra & Symbolic Mathematics (SymPy)

### Background
SymPy is Python's premier open-source library for symbolic mathematics, used across academic research, quantum physics pipelines, and engineering design. Soham Vyas has 4 officially merged pull requests in the matrix expressions engine, all personally reviewed and merged by core maintainer S.Y. Lee.

### KroneckerProduct Exponentiation & Powers (PR #31284)
- **Primary Upstream Source**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/31284
- **Related Issue**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/issues/31272 (Authored by Soham Vyas, resolved and closed)
- **Problem**: In matrix expressions, computing powers of Kronecker products `KroneckerProduct(A, B)**p` produced unevaluated generic `MatPow` objects even when factors were square matrices and powers were concrete or symbolic integers.
- **Mathematical Solution**: Applied the mixed-product exponentiation identity:
  $$(A \otimes B)^p = A^p \otimes B^p \quad \forall p \in \mathbb{Z}$$
- **Implementation**: In `sympy.matrices.expressions.kronecker`, implemented `_eval_power(exp)` to distribute integer exponents across square factor matrices, and evaluate identity matrix for $p = 0$.
- **Verification**: Verified and merged into `sympy/sympy:master` (commit `9f404e5`).

### KroneckerProduct ZeroMatrix Canonicalization (PR #31207)
- **Primary Upstream Source**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/31207
- **Problem**: ZeroMatrix tensor factors in Kronecker products retained unsimplified tensor blocks and failed fuzzy boolean evaluations.
- **Mathematical Solution**: $A \otimes 0_{m \times n} = 0_{rows \times cols}$
- **Implementation**: Canonicalized zero-matrix factor products with post-flattening factor extraction and fuzzy boolean matrix checks.
- **Verification**: Verified and merged into `sympy/sympy:master` (commit `004d908`).

### KroneckerProduct.trace() Optimization (PR #31011)
- **Primary Upstream Source**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/31011
- **Problem**: In matrix tensor products, computing the trace of $A \otimes B$ traditionally resulted in explicit expansion into an $nm \times nm$ block matrix, which scales at $O(n^3 m^3)$ in time and consumes catastrophic amounts of memory for large or symbolic dimensions. Furthermore, when rectangular sub-factors were evaluated, SymPy threw `NonSquareMatrixError`.
- **Mathematical Solution**: Utilizes the canonical property:
  $$\text{tr}(A \otimes B) = \text{tr}(A) \cdot \text{tr}(B)$$
- **Implementation**: In `sympy.matrices.expressions.kronecker`, added an explicit `.trace()` dispatch that rewrites the trace as `Mul(*[Trace(factor) for factor in expr.args])`. Rectangular factors are guarded by asserting total square dimension compatibility.
- **Verification**: Verified and merged into `sympy/sympy:master`.
- **Canonical Article**: https://www.soham.lol/blog/sympy-kronecker-trace/

### MatrixUnit.trace() Fix (PR #31010)
- **Primary Upstream Source**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/31010
- **Problem**: For elementary matrices $E_{i,j}$ where a single coordinate is 1 and all other coordinates are 0, computing $\text{Trace}(E_{i,j})$ returned 0 even when $i = j$.
- **Mathematical Solution**: $\text{tr}(E_{i,j}) = \delta_{i,j}$ (the Kronecker delta).
- **Implementation**: In `sympy.matrices.expressions.matexpr`, evaluated `MatrixUnit.trace()` as `KroneckerDelta(i, j)`.
- **Verification**: Verified and merged into `sympy/sympy:master`.

### MatrixBase Hermitian/Antihermitian Squareness Guard (PR #31303)
- **Primary Upstream Source**: https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/31303
- **Related Issue**: Fixes Bug H13 from Maintainer Issue https://github.com/sympy/sympy/issues/31291
- **Problem**: Non-square matrices in `Q.hermitian` and `Q.antihermitian` queries caused mathematical errors: tall matrices (3x2) erroneously evaluated to `True`, while wide matrices (2x3) crashed with `IndexError`.
- **Implementation**: In `sympy.assumptions.handlers.sets`, added explicit `if not mat.is_square: return False` to both `HermitianPredicate` and `AntihermitianPredicate`.
- **Verification**: Verified and merged into `sympy/sympy:master` (commit `081d81e0`).

### Active Upstream Pull Requests
- **PR #31232**: `assumptions: register KroneckerProduct in matrix predicate handlers` (29/29 CI checks passing).

## 2. Distributed Systems & High-Throughput Rate Limiting

### AI Rate Limiter Shield
- **Core Architecture**: Atomic sliding-window rate limiter utilizing Redis Sorted Sets (ZSETs) executed via Lua.
- **Why Multi-Step Redis Fails**: Traditional multi-step approaches (e.g. separate `ZREMRANGEBYSCORE`, `ZCARD`, and `ZADD` commands) suffer from race conditions under high concurrency where simultaneous requests read stale counter states before writes complete.
- **Atomic Lua Solution**:
  1. `redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, current_time - window_size)`
  2. `local count = redis.call('ZCARD', key)`
  3. If `count < limit`, execute `redis.call('ZADD', key, current_time, request_id)` and return `1`.
  4. If `count >= limit`, return `0` (triggering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests).
- **ML Anomaly Layer**: Scikit-Learn Isolation Forest monitors request burst velocity, client entropy, and IP distribution to isolate coordinated botnets without impacting legitimate traffic.
- **Dedicated Page**: https://www.soham.lol/projects/ai-rate-limiter-shield/
- **Canonical Article**: https://www.soham.lol/blog/redis-lua-rate-limiter/

## 3. Cryptographic Security & Information Theory

### Cybersecurity Risk Analyzer
- **Information Theory**: Claude Shannon's 1948 paper *A Mathematical Theory of Communication* defines information entropy as:
  $$H(X) = -\sum_{i=1}^{n} P(x_i) \log_2 P(x_i)$$
  For password and token secret strength, theoretical entropy is bounded by:
  $$E = L \log_2 R$$
  where $L$ is string length and $R$ is the size of the character pool.
- **Brute Force Estimation**: Simulates adversary capabilities against dedicated modern GPU clusters capable of $10^{11}$ hashes/sec (100 GH/s) using NTLM and bcrypt penalty factors.
- **NIST SP 800-63B Compliance vs. Mathematical Entropy**: NIST SP 800-63B emphasizes length (minimum 8 characters, recommended >= 15 for privileged access), checking against compromised credential corpuses, and eliminating artificial composition rules (e.g. requiring special characters); Claude Shannon's entropy models the theoretical search space and brute-force complexity under GPU cluster dictionary exhaustion models.
- **Dedicated Page**: https://www.soham.lol/projects/cybersecurity-risk-analyzer/
- **Canonical Article**: https://www.soham.lol/blog/shannon-entropy-cybersecurity/
